clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country in March 1952, the family's balance shifted over the following year. June became homesick and anxious, writing to her sister daily; Walter spent long hours away in the orchard, and the two grew distant. Glen got into fights at his new school. Walter stopped writing to his brother Harlan after a quarrel over their father's land. June's functioning fell—she kept to her bed for weeks that winter—and Walter and June clashed over money for new trees. By September 1953, June had joined the church choir and her letters thinned out, her anxiety easing and her functioning rising.

clusters.name: The orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when the late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan, the family's balance tilted. Walter began drinking heavily, and he and Glen blamed each other. Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank, overfunctioning under the strain. Glen's son Carl's asthma attacks grew worse that winter. Nora, eight years old, began wetting the bed again in April 1969. Ida's heart trouble was found around the same time. By October 1969, Walter had stopped drinking and taken work pruning other men's trees, his functioning rising.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's job loss in February 1975 when the Ridgeport cannery closed, the household's stability cracked. Glen sat out of work most of that year in his truck in the yard, his functioning down. He and Marian fought loudly over money at night, and Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night, overfunctioning. Nora stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer; she kept to her room and withdrew from her mother. Walter began drinking again after six years off it in December. By June 1976, when Glen started driving a delivery truck, Nora was eating again and had made the track team, her functioning rising.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora and Hollis's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma moving into Nora and Hollis's house in January 1990, the household erupted. Nora and Wilma clashed over the children's bedtimes and meals. Hollis worked late and kept out of the rows, drawing away from Nora, while he turned toward his mother. Owen began having tantrums at preschool and was sent home twice. Wilma took over Lily's care, overfunctioning in the household. Nora's eczema flared on both hands, and she and Hollis had rows most nights. Marian drove over twice a week to take Nora's side. When Wilma moved to a flat in town in June 1991, Nora's eczema cleared over the summer.

declined.reason: The wildfire in August 1994 lasted four days—from the evacuation to the return home—with the family calm again within a week. An acute episode around a real threat, not a period.

Two of the three shifts that count are told as how things always were or with lasting complaint language: Tess's drinking in October 1996 and Marian's overfunctioning in January 1997 are not departures from ordinary level. One shift alone—Nora's anxiety rising in November 1996—is a reaction, and no change in the family on a known date sits among these events; not enough in the diagram to choose a reading.
